note.en: Landmarks to confirm: Cavity of right atrium

steps.en: What you see: The right atrium, the tricuspid valve with its anterior and septal leaflets, and the crescent of the right ventricle lie in one plane. The inferior vena cava enters the atrium from below on the right of the image.
Landmarks to confirm: Do not accept the view until each of these is on screen.
Common mistakes and how to correct them: Each mistake below comes from the view catalogue with its correction.
Normal values: Tricuspid regurgitation peak velocity 2.8 m per s or less is normal.
Right atrial pressure reads near 3 mmHg when the cava is 21 mm or less with collapse above 50 percent.
Pulmonary pressure estimate equals 4 times the velocity squared plus right atrial pressure.

Pitfalls: The normal tricuspid annulus sits slightly nearer the apex than the mitral annulus, so do not call this small offset an Ebstein anomaly. Run colour across the valve in every study, since functional regurgitation is common when the right heart dilates.
Indian context: Rheumatic fever can scar the tricuspid valve as well as the mitral valve, so a young Indian patient with mitral stenosis deserves a careful tricuspid look in this view.

Common mistakes and how to correct them: Drifting medial into a standard long axis that hides the tricuspid valve. Correct it by tilting toward the right hip again until the tricuspid leaflets fill the centre.
Losing the inferior vena cava junction by fanning too anterior. Correct it by fanning posteriorly until the cava walls run straight into the atrium.
Confusing a prominent Eustachian ridge with a mass. Correct it by watching it through the cycle, since the ridge moves with the atrial wall while a mass does not.

todo.en: How to get it: Place the probe at left sternal edge, fourth intercostal space, tilted to the right hip.
Point the probe marker toward the right shoulder, about ten o clock.
From the long axis, tilt the tail of the probe toward the right hip without sliding. If the aorta appears, you have tilted back toward the standard long axis.
Freeze the image only when every listed landmark is on screen at once.

remember.en: Spot a dilated right heart and a thickened tricuspid valve.

q.en: Which way do you tilt from the long axis to find right ventricular inflow?

why.en: Tilting toward the right hip opens the tricuspid valve and right heart.

q.en: A tricuspid velocity of 2.4 m per s with a small collapsible cava means what?

why.en: Velocity below 2.8 with low atrial pressure estimates a normal pressure.

q.en: The tricuspid annulus sits a little nearer the apex than the mitral annulus. What is this?

why.en: A small apical offset of the tricuspid valve is normal anatomy.
